core_summary: This chapter explores two-dimensional spatial measurement: Perimeter (1D boundary distance) and Area (2D enclosed surface region). Students master formulas for rectangles (P = 2(l + w), A = lw), squares (P = 4s, A = s^2), regular polygons (P = ns), and composite shapes. The chapter establishes unit conversions (1 m^2 = 10,000 cm^2; 1 hectare = 10,000 m^2) and explores conservation of area under shape cutting/re-arrangement versus perimeter variation. Students prove that among all rectangles with a fixed area, a square minimizes perimeter, and apply concepts to real-world fencing, tiling, flooring, and landscaping problems.
key_concepts: Perimeter Definition and Formulas: Perimeter is the total continuous boundary distance around a closed 2D plane shape. Formulas: Rectangle P = 2(l + w); Square P = 4s; Regular n-gon P = n x s.

Area Definition and Formulas: Area measures the magnitude of two-dimensional surface region enclosed within a closed boundary, expressed in square units (sq cm, sq m). Formulas: Rectangle A = l x w; Square A = s^2.
1D Linear vs. 2D Surface Measurement: Perimeter measures 1D outer boundary length (cm, m), while Area measures 2D enclosed surface space (sq cm, sq m).
Square Unit Conversions: Converting 2D area units requires squaring 1D conversion factors: 1 m = 100 cm => 1 m^2 = 100 cm x 100 cm = 10,000 cm^2. 1 hectare = 10,000 m^2.

Area Conservation under Shape Rearrangement: Cutting a 2D shape into sub-pieces and rearranging them conserves total surface area (Total Area = sum of piece areas), whereas the outer perimeter boundary length can change dramatically.

Perimeter Variation under Fixed Area: Different rectangular shapes can share identical surface areas while having completely different perimeters. Among all rectangles with a fixed area A, a square minimizes perimeter.

Composite Shape Decomposition: Calculating the area of complex irregular or L-shaped figures involves decomposing the shape into non-overlapping simple rectangles, computing individual areas, and summing them.

Grid Square Area Estimation: Estimating irregular shape areas on square grid paper: count fully enclosed squares as 1 sq unit, more-than-half squares as 1 sq unit, exactly half squares as 0.5 sq unit, and ignore less-than-half squares.

Cost Calculations for Fencing vs. Tiling: Fencing or border framing depends on boundary Perimeter (Cost = P x Rate/m). Flooring, tiling, painting, or turfing depends on surface Area (Cost = A x Rate/m^2).
Number of Tiles Formula: The total number of tiles needed to cover a floor = Floor Area / Tile Area (with matching units).
Regular Polygon Perimeter Property: For any regular polygon with n equal side lengths s, Perimeter P = n x s.
Optimization in Architectural Design: Understanding perimeter-area trade-offs helps architects minimize building perimeter (reducing material costs) while maximizing interior floor area.

key_terms.definition: The total continuous outer boundary distance surrounding a closed two-dimensional shape.
The magnitude of two-dimensional surface space enclosed within the boundary of a plane figure.
The standard unit for measuring area, representing the surface enclosed by a square with 1 unit side length.
A closed 2D shape with all side lengths equal and all interior angles equal.
A metric unit of land area equal to a square with 100 m side length (10,000 square meters).
A two-dimensional figure constructed by combining two or more basic geometric shapes.
The process of dividing a complex geometric figure into simpler non-overlapping shapes.
The mathematical principle stating that cutting and rearranging a shape leaves its total surface area unchanged.
Finding the shape dimensions that maximize area for a given perimeter, or minimize perimeter for a given area.
A technique for approximating irregular shape areas by counting unit grid squares.
The linear measurements of a shape, such as length, width, or side length.
The enclosing line or curve separating the interior region of a shape from its exterior.

key_takeaways: Perimeter measures 1D boundary distance (cm, m); Area measures 2D surface space (sq cm, sq m).
Rectangle Perimeter P = 2(l + w) and Area A = l x w; Square Perimeter P = 4s and Area A = s^2.
Perimeter of a regular n-gon = n x s.
1 sq m = 10,000 sq cm; 1 hectare = 10,000 sq m.
Cutting and rearranging a shape conserves total surface area, but can alter perimeter.
Among all rectangles with a fixed area, a square has the minimum perimeter.
Fencing and framing calculations use Perimeter; flooring, tiling, and painting use Area.
Number of floor tiles required = Total Floor Area / Single Tile Area.
Complex L-shaped figures are solved by decomposing into non-overlapping rectangles.
Grid counting estimates irregular surface areas by counting full and half unit squares.
